standard.title: Comma use
standard.description: understand how to use the comma for lists, to separate a dependent clause from an independent clause, and in dialogue
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use commas to indicate prepositional phrases, and apostrophes where there is multiple possession (AC9E5LA09). They have not yet systematically examined all three conventional comma uses — for lists, for separating clauses, and in dialogue.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students understand how the comma is used for lists, to separate a dependent clause from an independent clause, and in dialogue, and can apply these uses accurately in their own writing.

nodes.label: Three uses of the comma
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and explain the three main uses of the comma covered at Year 6: for lists, to separate a dependent clause from an independent clause, and in dialogue.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify which of the three comma uses applies in each of at least four provided sentences; explain the rule for each use in own words.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and explain all three comma uses in a range of example sentences; identify different uses of commas including between independent clauses with conjunctions in compound sentences.
wider: Analyse a professional writer's use of commas in a passage and classify each use, including noting any uses that go beyond the three taught
Research the Oxford comma debate and form a reasoned opinion about whether it should be used
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who treat commas as pause markers rather than grammatical signals apply them inconsistently in Nodes 2 and 3 — producing systematic punctuation errors in both controlled practice and extended writing.

response_modes.reason: Students commonly confuse clause-separation commas with list commas when encountering compound sentences. Encountering the three uses in diverse sentence contexts prevents the misconception that commas mark natural pauses rather than grammatical relationships.

success_criteria: Names the three comma uses covered at Year 6
Correctly identifies which use applies in at least three out of four provided examples

nodes.label: Applying comma use in writing
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use commas accurately for all three purposes in their own writing.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce at least three sentences — one demonstrating each comma use — with the comma placed correctly.
nodes.typical_width: Use commas accurately across all three purposes in extended writing; demonstrate comma use in dialogue correctly (including placement relative to speech marks and dialogue tags).
wider: Edit a provided passage with comma errors, correct them, and explain the reasoning behind each correction
Compare how dialogue punctuation conventions differ in different published texts and discuss whether authors sometimes deliberately break conventions
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot reliably place commas in controlled sentence production will not apply them accurately in the sustained composition required by Node 3 — errors established here propagate directly into extended writing.

response_modes.reason: Comma use requires precision through practice — students who understand the rules conceptually frequently revert to guessing or avoidance under the pressure of extended writing. Accuracy comes from repeated application in varied writing contexts.

success_criteria: Produces at least one sentence demonstrating each of the three comma uses correctly
Uses commas accurately in a short piece of own writing including at least one dialogue exchange

nodes.label: Comma accuracy in extended writing
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students use commas accurately across all three purposes consistently in extended writing across different text types.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a short piece of extended writing (including narrative or persuasive text with dialogue) in which commas are used accurately for at least two of the three purposes.
nodes.typical_width: Use commas accurately across all three purposes in extended writing across different text types (narrative, informative, persuasive); self-edit for comma accuracy as part of the writing process.
wider: Peer-edit a classmate's writing for comma accuracy, identifying and explaining any errors found
Analyse how published authors use commas in complex sentences and identify any comma choices that go beyond the three rules taught

response_modes.reason: Applying all three comma rules accurately under extended writing conditions requires integrating rule knowledge (Node 1) with production practice (Node 2) simultaneously — the integration pressure of composing and punctuating together is the learning challenge.

success_criteria: Uses commas accurately for at least two purposes in a piece of extended writing
Identifies and corrects at least one comma error in own or peer writing
